# TechnicalTask contract

## Purpose and source of truth

`technical-task.v1` is the canonical consumer contract for a verified practice
task. Consumers should not re-analyze prose or call an LLM to recover its goal,
result, concepts, plan, or verification semantics.

The existing `tz-authoring-candidate.v1` remains the single generated and
persisted source data in version 1. Its public `practice-task-blueprint.v1`
already owns the same normalized facts needed for a private Practice handoff. TZ Planner
therefore builds `TechnicalTaskV1` deterministically from that candidate rather
than asking the model for a duplicate object or storing the same facts twice.
For consumers, the resulting TechnicalTask is the authoritative aggregate; the
mapping below is stable and covered by round-trip tests.

## Version 1 shape

Every full task contains:

- `schema = technical-task.v1` and `schema_version = 1`;
- `goal`: the short semantic purpose of the task;
- `student_instruction`: only the public title, description, requirements,
  roles, constraints, and non-goals;
- `expected_result`: one discriminated result contract;
- `concepts`: unique exact `(type, key, version)` learning targets and their
  role;
- `steps`: ordered semantic work units with dependencies, deliverables,
  concept/result/verification references, effort, and optional hints/actions;
- `verification`: proof contracts linked to expected-result IDs.

Unknown JSON fields, unsupported schema versions, unknown enum values, unsafe
paths, dangling references, duplicate IDs/orders/concepts, uncovered results,
and forward dependencies are rejected. Explicit `order` values are canonical:
decoding normalizes the step slice into that order. Step dependencies must
refer to earlier steps. An explicit milestone dependency requires every step
of the prerequisite milestone to precede every step of the dependent
milestone; otherwise independent milestones may interleave through their
step-level DAG. Expected results must both be assigned to a step and covered by
at least one verification contract.

`expected_result` is a closed discriminated union in schema v1. It supports the
current `acceptance_contract` plus typed `http_endpoint`, `cli_command`, `file`,
`database_state`, `function_behavior`, `api_contract`, `ui_state`,
`test_result`, `process`, `service`, `architecture`, and `other` families. The
last state/behavior families use structured assertions rather than prose-only
values. New representations require a new compatible schema version rather
than silently changing v1 semantics.

Verification is intentionally distinct from the expected result:

- the expected result states what must exist or work;
- verification states how a consumer proves that outcome.

A verification item has one source of execution semantics: either a bounded
inline HTTP/command/file contract or an `execution_contract_ref` into the
verified private evaluation bundle. It cannot have both.

## Deterministic mapping from the generated candidate

The one schema-constrained model response supplies all semantic facts:

- `blueprint.scenario.goal` -> `goal`;
- `blueprint.scenario` and `blueprint.source.educational_adaptation` ->
  `student_instruction`;
- `blueprint.acceptance` -> `expected_result.acceptance_contract`;
- all `milestones.steps.learning_requirements` -> unique exact `concepts`;
- milestone/step DAGs -> a stable flattened step order with milestone metadata;
- validator checks and review rules -> `verification`.

`educational_adaptation` is the preferred student-facing description. Legacy
candidates may omit it, in which case the projection uses the first public
scenario requirement. It never substitutes the internal pedagogical `goal`
into student-visible prose.

When the same concept has several learning policies, the aggregate keeps the
strongest role: `required`, `practiced`, `adaptive`, `recommended`, then
`optional`. Existing authoring policies currently generate `required`,
`recommended`, `adaptive`, or `optional`; `practiced` is reserved for a future
compatible producer.

Hints are a bounded ordered list of levels 1–7. Actions are optional and limited
to semantic notes, commands, or safe workspace file operations. Neither field
is required to represent a valid semantic step, and neither is exposed by the
student view. These types are extension points for AI Teacher, deterministic
agents, walkthroughs, and replay; TZ Planner does not execute them.

## Persistence and backward compatibility

READY jobs already persist the normalized candidate and private verification
receipt in `tz_authoring_job.artifact_json`. Version 1 deliberately adds no
second JSONB column and no relational copy of steps or concepts:

- jobs are queried by job/idempotency/state/lease fields, not by task concepts
  or step IDs;
- Practice owns the relational Family/Variant/Revision/Step catalog;
- duplicating the blueprint-derived task would introduce consistency and digest
  risks;
- polymorphic result and verification details fit the existing versioned
  artifact boundary.

Loading an old READY `artifact_json` and applying the deterministic projection
produces the same `technical-task.v1`; therefore no data backfill or migration
is required. If TZ Planner later owns concept/step queries, that access pattern
must justify a separate migration and normalized indexes instead of ad-hoc JSON
searches.

## Read models and confidentiality

`GET /internal/v1/authoring-jobs/{id}/technical-task` returns the full aggregate
for trusted internal consumers and is available only for READY jobs.

`GET /internal/v1/authoring-jobs/{id}/student-view` returns
`student-technical-task-view.v1`. Its Go type contains only schema metadata and
`student_instruction`; goal, concepts, steps, hints, actions, verification,
private evaluation, reference files, and negative fixtures cannot be serialized
through that type.

The quality gate also rejects verbatim reference-file content if it appears as
a complete public field, as a substantive substring, or as a compact
code-shaped snippet in the public instruction. This covers short reference
solutions without treating arbitrary one-character overlap as a leak. It is a
defense-in-depth check, not a substitute for the structural DTO boundary.

## Generation policy

AI Prompt receives one confidential request using
`practice-task.authoring-candidate.v1@2`. Its server-owned `authoring_policy`
contains the `technical-task.v1` field boundaries and mapping rules, together
with tone `supportive_direct`, methodology `incremental_evidence_first`, and the
versioned authoring skills. After the single structured response, ordinary Go
code performs normalization, projection, domain validation, exact catalog
resolution, and verification. UI views, sorting, and DTO mapping never trigger
another model call.

The contract intentionally does not implement a video renderer, TTS, browser
automation, code execution, a full AI Teacher, or a general workflow DSL.
